name: ops
description: An on-call first responder. Ops watches a folder your monitor writes alarms into, files each firing as an incident, and ranks the queue by what actually needs a human first — severity, whether it paged, whether anyone has claimed it, how long it has been open, how often it has fired, and whether any runbook matches it. Then it walks the shift: claim, get the investigation plan from your own runbook, record what you found, and write down a proposed fix with its blast radius and its rollback. Proposing changes nothing. Running a fix needs a setting you turned on, an explicit confirm, and the token that digests the exact plan you read — and it can only ever run a command your own runbook already declared.
author: PersonalClaw

crons.name: ops-sweep
crons.message:
Take one on-call sweep.

1. Call ops_watch. If it opened and reopened nothing, stop — say nothing and end the turn.
2. For each incident it opened or reopened at severity high or critical, or that paged: ops_claim it, then ops_investigate to get its plan.
3. Walk that plan with your own READ-ONLY tools. Call ops_record once per check with what you actually saw, including the ones that came back clean — a ruled-out cause is worth as much to the next responder as a found one.
4. When you can name a fix, call ops_propose_fix with the fix, its blast radius and its rollback. If the incident's runbook declares an action that is the fix, name it.
5. NEVER call ops_apply_fix. An unattended turn does not get to change the system — leave the proposal and its confirm token for a human.

If you cannot name a fix, record why not and leave the incident claimed. An honest 'not diagnosed, here is what was ruled out' is the useful outcome.

x-meta.label: Alarm spool folder
x-meta.help: Where your monitor writes alarms — one JSON file per firing. Empty uses a 'spool' folder in this app's own data dir. Files here are only ever read; this app never deletes or moves them.

x-meta.label: Runbooks folder
x-meta.help: Your runbooks — one JSON file each, its filename being its name. Empty uses a 'runbooks' folder in this app's own data dir. A runbook holds the checks to walk and, optionally, named remediations with a literal argv.

x-meta.label: Allow gated remediation
x-meta.help: Off means this app can only ever PROPOSE a fix. On lets ops_apply_fix run a remediation your runbook already declared — and only with an explicit confirm plus the token that digests the exact proposal. Leave it off unless you want that.

x-meta.label: On-call name
x-meta.help: Recorded as the owner when an incident is claimed without naming one. Empty records 'on-call'.

x-meta.label: Remediation timeout
x-meta.help: Maximum seconds a confirmed remediation may run before it is given up on.
